name: Teydea Site Assistant – Site Health Checklist, Audit & Setup Wizard
author: Teydea Studio

sections.description:
Teydea Site Assistant is a site health checklist for WordPress. It checks how your site is set up and shows each finding as a card you can act on.

Each card says what it found, why that matters and what you can do about it. Some fix the problem with one click, some walk you through a short flow, and some link to the WordPress screen where the setting lives.

Key benefits:

  • See setup, security, SEO, performance, content, operations and compliance checks on one screen.
  • Get a score from 0 to 100, overall and for each category, that moves as you work through the cards.
  • Fix common problems from the card that found them, when you choose to.
  • Keep your data on your site: checks run on your server, and your WordPress sends the digest.

The plugin checks practices, not products. When something your host or another plugin may handle, such as backups or two-factor sign-in, leaves no trace the plugin can read, you can mark the card handled.

Features

The card screen

  • Overview with a score. “Site Assistant” → “Overview” shows the overall score and its change since the last check, a tab per category with its own score, and the cards that need attention first.
  • Checks run in the background. “Check now” runs every check, “Check again” runs one card, and you can select several cards to run together.
  • Your decisions about a card. Snooze a card for 7, 30 or 90 days, dismiss it, mark it handled when the practice is covered elsewhere, or mark it not applicable. Every decision can be undone.
  • History. Each card keeps its results from the runs you keep, so you can see when something started failing.
  • Dashboard widget. The score and the top three recommendations on the WordPress Dashboard.

The checks

  • Setup: search engine visibility, site tagline, time zone, permalinks, sample content, logo and site icon, login page branding, site navigation, recommended theme plugins, email sending.
  • Security: the “admin” login, password policy, dormant accounts, number of administrators, two-factor authentication for administrators, login attempt limiting, theme and plugin file editors, abandoned plugins, plugins closed on WordPress.org, logins visible to visitors, inactive plugins and themes.
  • SEO: basic meta tags on the front page, sitemap, robots.txt, Search Console and analytics.
  • Performance: page cache, PHP version, persistent object cache, database cleanup, autoloaded options.
  • Content: stale content, oversized images in the media library, addresses that answer “not found”.
  • Operations: backups, pending updates, scheduled tasks, Site Health critical issues.
  • Compliance: privacy policy page, imprint page.

Fixes

  • One-click fixes, such as turning off the file editors, moving the sample content to the trash, or cleaning up old revisions and spam comments. A fix that deletes data asks you to confirm first.
  • Guided flows for changes that need your input, such as renaming the “admin” login, writing a tagline, creating a privacy policy draft, or choosing which inactive plugins to delete.
  • Links to the WordPress screen that already handles the setting.
  • Plugin installs from WordPress.org, offered by a few cards for a plugin by Teydea Studio or one your theme recommends.

Weekly email digest

Off until you turn it on. Once a week it mails up to 10 addresses the score, how it moved, what needs attention and what was fixed. You choose the weekday and time, and can send a test mail first.

Settings

“Site Assistant” → “Settings” holds the digest, how many check runs to keep (10 by default, up to 25), and the two security settings the file editor and login visibility fixes turn on, so you can turn them off.

Setup wizard

When the active theme supports it, “Site Assistant” → “Setup wizard” sets a fresh site up the way the theme’s demo looks: the plugins the theme offers, optionally the demo’s pages and images, and the colors, fonts, site title and logo you pick. Nothing is imported or changed until you start it. Importing content is cleared by default on a site that already has some, and the wizard warns you before the import replaces the page your site shows first.

Privacy

The plugin stores this personal data, all of it in your site’s own database:

  • when each account last signed in, recorded on every sign-in for the dormant accounts check and listed in its results, included in WordPress’s personal data export and erasure tools;
  • the paths of requests that answered “not found”, without the query string, and the hosts of the pages that linked to them, at most 1,000 paths, recorded while the “not found” card is open or snoozed;
  • the email addresses the weekly digest goes to, and when a copy to one could not be sent;
  • a note on an author’s account when you choose to keep their profile address;
  • each administrator’s preferences on the plugin’s screens, such as hiding passing checks.

None of it is sent to Teydea Studio or any other service. Suggested text for your privacy policy is under Settings → Privacy. Deleting the plugin removes its tables, the digest’s settings and the data above except the author note; other settings stay.

External services

Demo site (setup wizard only). The wizard reads its demo content from demo.teydeastudio.com, run by Teydea Studio. Three kinds of request go to the demo host, and none signs in or sends an account, a key, or content read from your site:

  • the demo’s pages, loaded by your browser into the wizard’s preview only once you choose the live preview over the theme’s pictures; your choices, including the site title and logo, reach the preview inside your browser, without a request;
  • the demo’s content, fetched by your site with a GET request when you open “See exactly what arrives” or start the import;
  • the images that content names, checked with a HEAD request and downloaded into your media library during the import.

The last two carry WordPress’s standard User-Agent header, with the WordPress version and your site’s address. None of them happens on a schedule or in the background.

Terms: https://teydeastudio.com/terms-and-conditions/ Privacy policy: https://teydeastudio.com/privacy-policy/

Plugin installs from WordPress.org. The wizard and a card’s install button use WordPress’s own installer, which asks WordPress.org about the plugin by its slug and downloads its ZIP file.

Plugin directory lookups. The “Abandoned plugins” and “Plugins closed on WordPress.org” checks look your active plugins up at api.wordpress.org. Each GET request names up to ten plugins by folder or file name, which can include a plugin that did not come from WordPress.org unless its Update URI header names another host. Answers are kept on your site for a day.

PHP version check. It asks WordPress.org, through WordPress’s own function, which PHP version it recommends for yours, and keeps the answer for a week.

None of these WordPress.org requests signs in or sends anything else read from your site, and each carries the User-Agent header above. WordPress.org privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

The “Site Health critical issues” check runs WordPress’s own Site Health tests, one of which checks that your site can reach WordPress.org. Checks such as the sitemap, robots.txt and page cache cards request your own site’s pages as a visitor would, following its redirects, and the background queue makes requests to your site.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the teydea-site-assistant directory to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin on the “Plugins” screen.
  3. Open “Site Assistant” in the admin menu and press “Run the first check”.
  4. Work through the cards that need attention, and turn on the weekly digest if you want a summary by email.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin change my site without asking?

No. Checks read the site and change nothing. They never run on a schedule, only when you start them, after a fix, and when you change the search engine visibility setting. The weekly digest only reports the latest results.

A fix runs only when you press its button, and one that deletes data asks you to confirm first. Two cards record data as the site is used, described under Privacy.

Does it send my data anywhere?

The checks run on your own server, and the digest is sent by your own WordPress to the addresses you enter. The plugin contacts an outside service only in the cases listed under “External services” below: the theme’s demo site while you use the setup wizard, and WordPress.org for plugin installs and three checks.

What does the score mean?

It is the share of counted checks that pass, from 0 to 100, with each check weighted low, medium or high. A card you mark handled counts as passing.

Snoozed and dismissed cards, and checks that do not apply or could not run, are left out. The score measures these checks only and is not a guarantee that a site is secure or fast.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes, per site. Each site has its own screen, checks, score and digest, even when network-activated.

Where can I find the unminified source code?

All source ships with the plugin: the plugin’s own JavaScript is in src/, and the bundled @teydeastudio/components and @teydeastudio/utils libraries are in deps/js/components/src/ and deps/js/utils/src/. To rebuild, install Node.js 24 and run npm install && npm run build in the plugin directory.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1 (2026-11-13)

  • The setup wizard asks before it loads the live preview from the demo site, and offers the theme’s screenshots instead
  • The settings screen keeps a history of saved settings, which can be restored
  • Applying a look in the setup wizard no longer overwrites a Site Editor save made at the same moment
  • The 404 monitor counts every first visit from a referring site, including two that arrive at once
  • Old scheduled-task records are cleaned up in smaller batches
  • Dependencies updated
  • Code improvements

1.0.0 (2026-11-09)

  • The first stable release

(For older records, see the changelog.txt file).
